parts.t: Aldergrove is on the Township’s eastern border, with a mix of rural, residential and business use. The Township describes it as a small urban-rural community. It has its own community centre and pools, a large regional park and a border crossing to the U.S.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 8, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Township of Langley.

Aldergrove has its own community plan, with a core area plan for the town centre.
The Aldergrove Community Plan (Bylaw No. 1802) was adopted by Council on January 8, 1979.
The plan includes an Aldergrove Core Area Plan for about 80 acres centred on Fraser Highway and 272 Street.
The core area plan expects a future population of about 6,650 people by 2041.
Rural land outside the urban area falls under the Rural Plan, and most of the rural area is in the ALR.

Is there a border crossing in Aldergrove?
Yes. The Aldergrove port of entry on Highway 13 is open daily from 8am to midnight, with NEXUS lanes into Canada from noon to 8pm.

Is there an off-leash dog area?
Aldergrove Regional Park has an off-leash area off Lefeuvre Road.
